guest.bio_context: Ray Smith spent nearly 30 years in the music industry starting around 1975-1976, working as a roadie, manager, and tour manager for major acts including Johnny Diesel and the Injectors, Cold Chisel, the Rolling Stones, Joe Cocker, and Oasis. He transitioned to the construction industry where he became a delegate representing union members, experiencing the full range of construction work including mixed metals, civil engineering, building, and infrastructure projects across Melbourne and regional Victoria.

Johnny Diesel and the Injectors: first band in Australia to sell half a million copies

pending_qa.q: How did Ray Smith manage high-profile touring artists and what challenges did he encounter?
pending_qa.r: Ray toured with major international acts including the Rolling Stones and Joe Cocker, becoming good friends with Cocker who would ring him whenever he toured Australia. Ray was Oasis's Australian tour manager during their early tour, and had to manage a Gallagher brother who was disruptive at Sydney Entertainment Centre. Ray ultimately decided to leave touring because of the constant airports, tour buses, planes, trains, and everything in between, which took him a long time to recover from.

pending_qa.q: What approach did Ray Smith take when confronted with disrespectful behavior from a touring artist?
pending_qa.r: When a Gallagher brother from Oasis was carrying on rudely at Sydney Entertainment Centre about the third night of their tour, Ray politely bumped him into a room and said: if we're going to work together, you're going to learn to be a bit more respectful in the way you talk to people. I don't know how you talk to your old man, but you won't be talking to me like that. The artist's London management later praised Ray for being the first to pull the artist in line, and the next day the artist apologized.
